items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: the band -- it was a gasser. Like the union had a beef about something there, and the guy came in and heard the band -- Vincent Battali or something like that -- he said, 'Oh, I couldn't do anything to hurt this band.' He said -- and they actually figured out a way to circumvent their own

ctx.x: Yeah, horrible. An awful joint. But the only reason I went in there at all was Basin Street wanted me back with the big band, and I wanted to go to New York one more time, and Clarke and I had a pact, and Nat Pierce, and we had talked about it. I said, "If I can get Basin Street we're going to do this and we'll do that." It

was all agreed. So I called them and I said, 'All right, I've got the deal set. Are you guys still ready to go?' 'Yeah.' So I wanted a place to reacclimate myself to being in front of a band, and The Chez presented that, the feeling of leading a band, and also the mechanics of it. Because you forget, you get away from it, you know, I had to learn my own arrangements over again, plus put a lot of new ones in, which I did. And we played there two weeks, and business was not good. But I took Willie Smith with me.…
